newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS - S-E-Banken profit soars, loan losses slump.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - S-E-Banken profit soars, loan losses slump.

text.p: Swedish commercial bank S-E-Banken on Tuesday reported a leap in profits for the first nine months of 1996 as income rose sharply and loan losses fell by two thirds.
The operating profit of the banking arm of the Wallenberg industrial empire was more than doubled to 4.42 billion crowns ($670 million) from the 2.06 billion posted for the same period last year.
The 115 percent profit surge was mainly the result of a slump in loan losses to 1.23 billion crowns ($186.4 million) from 3.61 billion crowns in the corresponding period in 1995.
Lending losses now correspond to just 0.65 percent of the total loan portfolio, whilst doubtful claims declined 42 percent to a net of 4.78 billion crowns.
But the improvement in the bank's performance was not just the result of a continuing decline in losses on bad loans and real estate of dubious value.

Top line earnings were also strongly ahead as interest costs fell seven percent to 16.89 billion crowns and interest income declined just three percent to 22.10 billion for an interest net of 5.44 billion crowns, including leasing income.

"This increase is mainly explained by falling market rates, which led to an improved yield on the bank's bond portfolios and to lower costs of financing the bank's problem assets, mainly Diligentia," S-E-Banken said in a statement.

Property unit Diligentia was spun off to shareholders earlier this year in a move that marked an end to the bank's unwilling involvement in the real estate market following the property crash in Sweden in the early 1990s.
Commission on retail and investment banking operations was also strongly ahead, with commission income minus costs contributing 3.43 billion crowns to consolidated earnings.
The only blemish on an otherwise strong interim report was a 12 percent rise in personnel costs to 3.93 billion crowns, despite a fall in total staff numbers.

Even though the bank's profits came in ahead of the market consensus forecast of 4.17 billion crowns, the share did not move from its level of 56.50 crowns immediately prior to the publication of the figures.
Analysts said although there were no real surprises in the report, the figures came as further proof that the bank had returned to financial health.

"It's looking good for the next couple of years with strong levels of profitability, and that should continue unless anything drastic happens in the economy," Steven Lewis of UBS in London told Reuters.
"The longer term question is what they do strategically."
One strategic development expected by many industry analysts is a concentration of the sector as Sweden's big four banks move to take over smaller players.
Foreningsbanken, the country's fifth largest bank, is a potential victim, and the bank on Tuesday showed why larger preditors might be interested.
Foreningsbanken posted a seven percent rise in nine month operating profits to 811 million crowns ($123 million) compared with 758 million in the same period a year ago.
Credit losses, which included changes in value of property taken over, tumbled 31 percent to 750 million crowns while the bank's loan loss ratio fell to 1.1 percent from 1.7 percent.
The bank also announced a one billion dollar Euro Medium Term Notes programme to secure the bank's long-term borrowing on the capital market. The programme will be managed by Salamon brothers.
Shares in Foreningsbanken slipped 0.10 crowns to 26.90 crowns on a generally dull trading day in Stockholm.
S-E-Banken shares were one crown higher at 56.60 at 1500 GMT. ($=6.6070 Swedish crown)
